title: Avoiding Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Using a standard sanitary tee to join horizontal drain lines is a frequent code violation in drainage installation. Sanitary tees are engineered specifically for horizontal-to-vertical transitions. When installed in a flat horizontal run, the short sweep of a sanitary tee fails to direct waste solids smoothly down the line, resulting in splashing, flow retardation, and persistent clogs. Drainage codes require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-turn tee-wye for horizontal branch connections. Proper fitting selection maintains scouring velocity and ensures waste flows smoothly without back-pitching into connected branch lines.

Drainage codes require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-turn tee-wye for horizontal branch connections.
